s:
A company has a sales system that stores transactions as .csv files in an Amazon S3 bucket. The S3 bucket

is configured to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Most of the .csv files are between 64 KB and 100 KB in size. All rows and columns of the .csv files must be read when the data is processed. The company must keep the data for 5 years. The company stores several million xsv files every day. The company must minimize the cost of storing and querying the xsv files. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Create an AWS Glue job to convert the .csv files into Apache Parquet format. Use Amazon S3 to invoke the AWS Glue job every time a .csv file arrives.
Create an AWS Glue job to compress the .csv files. Schedule the AWS Glue job every hour to compress the files for the previous hour into one .csv file.
Create an AWS Lambda function to convert the .csv files into Apache Parquet format. Use Amazon S3 to invoke the Lambda function every time a .csv file arrives.
Create an AWS Lambda function to compress the .csv files. Use Amazon S3 to invoke the Lambda function every time a .csv file arrives.
e: To minimize costs for storing and querying millions of small CSV files: l Convert to Parquet format: Parquet is a columnar format that is highly compressed and optimized for analytical queries. For the scenario where 'all rows and columns must be read,' Parquet provides significant compression benefits over CSV, reducing storage costs and query costs. l S3 Intelligent-Tiering: Automatically moves objects between access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing costs for 5-year retention where access patterns may change l Amazon Athena for querying: Serverless SQL query service that works directly on S3 data. Pricing is based on data scanned; Parquet's compression and columnar format reduce data scanned per query, directly reducing query costs. No infrastructure to manage. l File size optimization: While original CSVs are 64-100 KB each, converting to Parquet in larger batches (combining multiple CSVs per Parquet file) further reduces overhead and improves query performance This solution minimizes both storage and query costs through format optimization, while S3 Intelligent-Tiering handles long-term cost optimization.

w.y: The deciding facts are millions of 64–100 KB files a day, all rows and columns read, and 'minimize the cost of storing and querying'. An hourly AWS Glue job that compresses each hour into one file cuts storage size, removes millions of tiny objects (which Intelligent-Tiering never moves out of the frequent tier when under 128 KB), and costs one job run per hour instead of millions.

o.A: Starting a Glue job for every file means millions of job runs a day, each billed for at least a minute, and Parquet's column pruning does not help when every column is read.
o.B: Correct: one scheduled Glue job per hour compresses and combines the files, cutting storage, object count and scan cost.
o.C: Cheaper than A per file, but still leaves millions of small objects and runs millions of Lambda invocations.
o.D: Still millions of tiny compressed objects, which keep per-object and request overhead and miss tiering savings.
